components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main action surface for download and install actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 12px; background: var(--accent, #4fb4ff); color: var(--bg, #080b14); padding: 0.85rem 1.75rem; font: 600 1rem/1.2 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(79, 180, 255, 0.4); transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1), filter 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 8px 20px rgba(79, 180, 255, 0.4); filter: brightness(1.1); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(246, 248, 255, 0.85); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Supporting action for GitHub Releases, TestFlight, README, or manual paths.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.15)); border-radius: 12px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05); color: var(--text, #f6f8ff); padding: 0.85rem 1.75rem; font: 600 1rem/1.2 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1), background 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1); border-color: var(--border-hover, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.3)); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent, #4fb4ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Feature Card
components.description: A compact proof card for a single capture capability.
components.html:
GIF Recording

Create animated GIFs with adjustable frame rate and max width for lightweight sharing.
components.css: .ds-card { border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.15)); border-radius: 16px; background: var(--bg-elevated, rgba(22, 30, 48, 0.6)); color: var(--text, #f6f8ff); padding: 1.75rem; transition: transform 0.3s ease, border-color 0.3s ease, background 0.3s ease, box-shadow 0.3s ease; } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); border-color: var(--border-hover, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.3)); background: rgba(30, 41, 59, 0.6); box-shadow: 0 20px 25px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2), 0 10px 10px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 0.75rem; font: 700 1.25rem/1.25 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--text-secondary, #a7b1cd); font: 400 0.95rem/1.6 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; }

components.name: Platform Tabs
components.description: The native segmented-control pattern for choosing macOS or Windows.
components.css: .ds-platform-tabs { display: inline-grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(160px, 1fr)); gap: 0.3rem; border: 1px solid var(--border-hover, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.3)); border-radius: 16px; padding: 0.3rem; background: rgba(16, 24, 42, 0.75); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04); } .ds-platform-tab { border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: var(--text-secondary, #a7b1cd); padding: 0.7rem 1.6rem; font: 600 1.05rem/1.2 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .ds-platform-tab:hover { color: var(--text, #f6f8ff); background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04); } .ds-platform-tab.is-active { color: var(--bg, #080b14); border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); background: var(--accent, #4fb4ff); box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(79, 180, 255, 0.4); } .ds-platform-tab:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent, #4fb4ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Command Line
components.description: Copyable install command treatment for Homebrew and winget.
components.css: .ds-command-line { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.55rem; } .ds-command-line code { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto; border: 1px solid var(--border-hover, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.3)); border-radius: 10px; background: rgba(79, 180, 255, 0.1); color: var(--code-text, #dce9ff); padding: 0.5rem 0.65rem; font-size: 0.86rem; } .ds-command-line button { border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.15)); border-radius: 10px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06); color: var(--text, #f6f8ff); padding: 0.45rem 0.7rem; font: 600 0.8rem/1.2 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s ease, border-color 0.2s ease; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-command-line button:hover { border-color: var(--border-hover, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.3)); background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); } .ds-command-line button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent, #4fb4ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Media Frame
components.description: Rounded product-image frame with subtle capture glow.
components.css: .ds-media-frame { margin: 0; border: 1px solid var(--border, rgba(140, 166, 219, 0.15)); border-radius: 20px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05); padding: 10px; box-shadow: 0 20px 25px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2), 0 10px 10px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), 0 0 80px rgba(79, 180, 255, 0.08); transition: transform 0.5s ease; } .ds-media-frame:hover { transform: scale(1.02); } .ds-media-placeholder { display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 220px; border: 1px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2); border-radius: 12px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(79, 180, 255, 0.16), rgba(8, 11, 20, 0.9)); color: var(--text, #f6f8ff); font: 700 1rem/1.4 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
Tiny Clips should feel like a compact creative tool sitting one click away: blue-lit, quiet, and immediately useful. The interface is dark because the product lives around screen capture and media work; the site should feel comfortable beside a Mac menu bar, a Windows tray, a video timeline, or a screenshot editor without turning into a theatrical developer console.

The system uses a focused cool palette, product imagery, rounded native-feeling controls, and restrained glow to communicate speed and capability. It rejects bloated enterprise SaaS marketing: no vague productivity murals, no fake metrics, no endless decorative feature grids, and no design moves that make a sub-5 MB utility feel like a subscription platform.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, blue-lit surfaces that make screenshots and video assets feel native.
Compact controls with clear platform choices and copyable install commands.
Ambient elevation: borders, tonal layers, and glow rather than heavy drop shadows.
Direct product proof through real app imagery, demo video, and exact install paths.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Capture Blue is the only saturated accent. Do not introduce a second accent hue for variety; use contrast, spacing, product imagery, or copy hierarchy instead.

rules.name: The Proof Over Decoration Rule
rules.body: Blue glow must attach to something functional: a button, selected tab, screenshot frame, or active state. Decorative glow without product meaning is forbidden.

rules.name: The Native Utility Rule
rules.body: Type should read like a polished native app, not a campaign poster. Avoid oversized display theatrics and keep copy scannable.

rules.name: The Sparse Label Rule
rules.body: One or two uppercase labels can orient the page; using them as section scaffolding across the whole site is forbidden.

rules.name: The Lift On Intent Rule
rules.body: Flat tonal surfaces are the default. Strong shadow, scale, and glow should appear only for interaction, media emphasis, or selected state.

rules.name: The No Arbitrary Z Rule
rules.body: Keep layering semantic: sticky header, lightbox overlay, lightbox content. Replace arbitrary values like `999` with a named z-index scale when touching related CSS.

dos: Do keep the site as lean as the product: every section needs concrete proof, a platform decision, or an install action.
Do use Capture Blue for action, selected state, and product proof; keep it rare enough to matter.
Do preserve real screenshots, videos, and app imagery as the main brand material.
Do write install and trust copy with exact platform details: Mac App Store, Homebrew, TestFlight, manual download, winget, GitHub Releases.
Do maintain WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, keyboard-friendly tab controls, visible focus states, and reduced-motion alternatives.
donts: Don't make Tiny Clips look like bloated enterprise SaaS marketing.
Don't ship generic AI landing-page polish: gradient-text hero effects, fake metrics, decorative glass cards, repeated tiny uppercase section labels, or endless identical feature grids.
Don't over-technicalize the brand. Command-line install paths are useful affordances, not the entire personality.
Don't add side-stripe borders, arbitrary z-index values, or purely decorative glow.
Don't introduce a second accent hue unless the product itself gains a real semantic need for it.
